newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece gratified by election calm in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Greece gratified by election calm in Albania.

text.p: Greece expressed satisfaction on Monday at the general calm that prevailed in Sunday's elections in neighbouring Albania and said the opposition Socialist party looked like the winner.
In Tirana, Albanian President Sali Berisha conceded the defeat of his Democratic Party.

"According to the first unofficial results it looks like the Socialist party is ahead. If these results are officially confirmed then it is a big success (for the Socialists) and we express our congratulations," Greek deputy foreign minister Yannos Kranidiotis said.
The Albanian Socialist party of Fatos Nano claimed to have won a resounding victory but no official results have so far been announced.

Nano, released from jail in March three years after what was widely considered a suspect trial, said on Sunday night his party's data showed it had won 60 of 115 seats contested under majority voting in the election.
Kranidiotis said Athens was happy that the elections took place in a generally calm environment and the Greek government looked forward for close ties with the new administration in Tirana.
"The government looks forward to close and productive relations with the new Albanian government in both political and development sectors," he said.
"Greece wants Albania to soon become a developed, prosperous and stable country and play an important role in the efforts for stability in the region."
Greece's Socialist government is known to have close ties with Nano and allowed him to hold an election rally in Athens earlier this month attended by thousands of Albanian immigrants in Greece.
Athens was often at odds with Albanian President Sali Berisha over the rights of a big Greek minority in southern Albania.
Athens newspapers fronted on Monday the Albanian election with headlines like "A new era for Albania" and "Berisha disappears."

Kranidiotis said Greek police were looking into the killing of a guard at the Greek consulate in the southern town of Gjirokaster early on Sunday, when youthful gunmen fired on the residence of the Greek consul.
Police said Christos Kollas was shot in the chest and died instantly.
